description: An AI packaging design generator turns one product photo into a realistic pack. Change the background and style in one line, then download the listing mockup.
h1: AI Packaging Design Generator for Listing Mockups
lead: Upload the pouch or box photo, name the pack style in one line, and download a square packaging design for the listing. Check it against the product you ship before anything is printed.

steps.d: Upload a clear photo of the box, pouch, or bottle you sell. That photo is what the packaging design is built from.
Say the pack style in one line, like a matte pouch. An avatar speaks that line only in a later clip.
Download the square packaging design and check it against the product. A tall crop can go to whoever runs the ads.

steps_h2: Make a Shelf Preview From One Package Photo in 3 Steps
steps_lead: A photo of the box or pouch starts it. You leave with a square packaging design the listing can use.

faq.q: What is an AI packaging design generator?
faq.a: An AI packaging design generator turns one product photo into a packaging design for the listing. You name the style, such as a matte box or a stand-up pouch, and download a square file. It is a picture of the pack you can check, not a printed dieline and not a filmed shelf ad.

faq.q: Do I need design skills to make a pack?
faq.a: No. You do not need a design job or a design degree to start. Upload the product photo and name the look in plain words. Publish the square file on the product page when it matches the pack you sell. Check the preview before you do.

faq.q: How does the packaging design tool work?
faq.a: Upload a photo of the box, pouch, or bottle, then name the style in one sentence, such as a cream label on a kraft box. The tool returns a square packaging design you can preview. Download it when the shape matches the product you ship.

faq.q: Can an online shop use the packaging design?
faq.a: Yes. A shop can use the design as the listing image or the product-page hero. Start from the box, pouch, or bottle you already sell, and check the shape against the real pack before you put the file up. Cosmetics, drinks, and other packed goods can all start this way.

faq.q: How long does a packaging design take?
faq.a: The preview comes back in the same sitting, so you are not booking a designer for that file. If a color is off, edit the style note and run it again from the same photo.

faq.q: Can I make designs for more than one product?
faq.a: Yes. Run each product from its own photo and a new style line. Use a cream box for one and a kraft pouch for the next. The products stay separate, and you download a square design for each listing. You are not rebuilding a shelf scene for every new item.

faq.q: Can I start from photos I already use?
faq.a: Yes. The product photo you already use on the listing is the right start. You can add up to 7 reference photos when you want the box, the pouch, and a close detail considered in the same design.

faq.q: Where can I place the finished design?
faq.a: Use the square design on the listing and the product page. If you also make a clip of that pack, TikTok takes the tall 9:16 file. A feed can take 1:1. A wide placement can take 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4.

faq.q: How much does a packaging design cost?
faq.a: You pay with a plan, not a design invoice. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A photo is 24 credits. A video, if you also make a clip, is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You see the spend before it runs, and a failed job puts those credits back.

faq.q: Can I use the design in ads and client work?
faq.a: Yes. Use the design on your listing, in a paid ad, or hand the file to a client whose product is in the photo. The download has no watermark, so you can place it where that product already sells.

faq.q: Why describe the pack instead of drawing it?
faq.a: You say the style in one line instead of building the pack in design software. A new product can keep the same kind of file, and only the style line changes, so you are not starting the layout over.

reviews.h2: How Shops Preview a Pack on a Shelf
reviews.lead: Example shelf scenes, from a coffee pack to a pouch. This is not a check of print color or the small legal words.

items.t: A finished shelf frame from one pack photo
items.d: Example: a coffee shop uploads the bag and gets a square cafe scene to judge before a print order.

items.t: The mockup and a clip in one project
items.d: Example: a tea shop makes the tin picture and a short product clip together, in one project, without a second app.

items.t: Start from the bottle photo or the link
items.d: Example: a sauce shop pastes the product page link, or uploads the bottle, and the preview keeps that bottle's shape.

items.t: An AI actor and captions on the clip
items.d: Example: the pouch stays the shelf picture. On the video, the shop picks an AI actor, a generated person, then adds words on screen.

items.t: The same jar scene in another language
items.d: Example: the wood-shelf still stays as it is, and the spoken line on the clip is recorded again for a second market.

items.t: A voiceover and a track on the clip
items.d: Example: the carton preview is for slides you show a store buyer. On the video, the editor adds a spoken voice and a track from the music library.

items.t: An AI actor instead of a filmed spot
items.d: Example: a supplement shop uses an AI actor, a generated person, to hold the pack. Small ingredient text can blur, so the real label photo keeps the wording.

items.t: A digital twin for the next bag
items.d: Example: a pet-food shop uses a digital twin, the same generated person, so the next bag clip matches the first. No new light setup.

items.t: A script, then a second version
items.d: Example: a juice shop pastes the product link, takes a short script, and compares two bottle versions in the same scene.

items.t: Publish the clip, or start from the API
items.d: Example: after a look at the sample print, the shop posts the clip to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram). The API lets the product list start the next box.
